patterns.what: 1978, the PSG: where the journey starts: a coin, then the theme on the PSG's square with a 50 Hz vibrato, each note let go just before the next and its long notes beeped in threes, as the old machines played, over the buzz bass (the PSG's envelope run as a waveform). From bar 5 the chords as 50 Hz arpeggios and the tone-and-noise drums. Then the time machine.

1983, the console: the adventure under way, in D, on the console's own four channels: the theme on the 25 % pulse with a late vibrato, turns and pick-ups filling its long notes; the other pulse its echo, three ticks behind and fading, then from bar 5 a third under it; the triangle's bass jumping octaves, and its kick; noise hats and snare through the console's filters.

1985, 16BIT: the dark chapter, the theme in B minor on the PSG's later version: its high notes held longer and a trill before the end, a square with a 50 Hz vibrato, itself as its echo; the sync-buzzer bass galloping; the chords as fast 50 Hz arpeggios all through; tone-and-noise drums, the kick on every beat.

1989, the handheld: the journey goes portable, in G, on the handheld's four channels: the theme high on one pulse sweeping its duty, with a late vibrato, playful with octave flicks and broken chords; the other pulse playing the chords as fast arpeggios, a new note every two rows; the wave channel's bass bouncing; the noise channel's hats and snare; the sweep kick.

the 2000s, all the chips: today's chip music, every chip at once, in A: the theme on the console's pulse, its phrases pushed an eighth early and ending on the top note, the handheld's pulse a third under it; the 16BIT fast arpeggios; the sync-buzzer bass; four on the floor on the triangle's kick, open hats on the off-beats, the console's snare; coins at the phrases' ends. Then the time machine heads home: a pulse sweeping down, the drums rolling on into the landing.

home: the landing and the way home: a crash, the 2000s' groove dying away over two bars on the handheld, the tempo slowing bar by bar from 160 to 108; the theme's last phrase at half speed, passed from the handheld to the 16BIT, to the console, to the PSG where it began, each bar in that era's variation, with its own chords, bass and kick; the last chord beeped and a coin.
